audit_scope.description: These subgraphs cover CL fork transitions (Electra-to-Fulu), CL validator duties (PeerDAS custody, sidecar distribution), and EL history expiry (EIP-7927). Both layers and their interfaces are in scope.

in_scope: PeerDAS validator custody and sidecar distribution (EIP-7594)

judging.severity_measurement: Impact on the entire Ethereum network
judging.poc_requirement_note: All submissions (except informational) must include an executable coded proof of concept at the time of submission

eips: EIP-7594: PeerDAS - Peer Data Availability Sampling
EIP-7823: Set upper bounds for MODEXP
EIP-7918: Blob base fee bounded by execution cost
EIP-7934: RLP Execution Block Size Limit
EIP-7935: Set default gas limit to XX0M
EIP-7951: Precompile for secp256r1 Curve Support

engine_api.description: EL-CL communication via Engine API is authenticated using JWT and considered semi-trusted
engine_api.rationale: Co-located EL and CL clients communicate via authenticated Engine API (JWT). The Engine API is considered a trusted boundary, but data returned by EL may not be fully verified by CL in all cases (e.g., blob data from engine_getBlobsV2 is used without KZG verification). If the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted data may be propagated to the network.
security_implications: Engine API is authenticated via JWT
Some data from EL may be used without full verification by CL
Compromised EL can affect CL behavior
engine_api.note: Vulnerabilities in Engine API implementation are in-scope, but attacks requiring a compromised local EL may be considered conditional or lower severity

local_validator.description: Local validator configuration is under operator control and considered semi-trusted
local_validator.rationale: Local validator configuration is under operator control. Misconfigured or manipulated validator settings could cause incorrect node behavior.
local_validator.note: Configuration issues requiring operator error are typically out-of-scope

p2p_peers.description: P2P network peers are unauthenticated and considered untrusted
p2p_peers.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary protocol messages. All P2P input must be fully validated.
p2p_peers.note: Vulnerabilities exploitable via P2P network are high priority for bug bounty

Critical.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Exploit an EIP/specification or client bug to easily create an infinite amount of ETH which is finalized by the network
Take down the entire network by sending a single malicious on-chain transaction that ends up crashing all clients
Critical.impact: Entire network (>50% validators or all clients)
Critical.attack_vector: Single malicious on-chain transaction or network packet

High.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 33% of the network
Bring down more than 33% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
High.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Medium.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 5% of the network
Bring down more than 5% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Medium.impact: More than 5% of the network (or >1% of validators for slashing)
Medium.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Low.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting at least 0.01% of the network
Bring down more than 0.01% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Low.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Informational.criteria: Observations or recommendations regarding code quality, maintainability, or system architecture that do not present a direct security risk
Informational.validity_requirement: Only applicable if the team decides to implement a change based on the report
notes: Informational issues are valid if they don't lead to a sufficient impact to count as Low or higher and are valuable enough for the client that they decided to implement the change in the code
Issues related to parts under the 'Out of scope' section will not be considered valid
Informational issues won't have duplicates, and only the first one is valid
They also don't qualify for the 1st and 2nd week multipliers, as they apply only to issues in the main pot

misclassified_entities.reason: Beacon Chain State is an internal component of the Consensus Layer, not an external entity. Validator effective balance is read from the local beacon state, not received from an external source.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Client via Beacon API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator client queries proposer lookahead duties via Beacon API. While typically co-located, Beacon API is explicitly out-of-scope per bug bounty. The validator client itself is semi-trusted (operator-controlled), but the API exposure is the concern. Marked UNTRUSTED as it is a network-accessible interface.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (GetPayloadResponse with BlobsBundle containing cell KZG proofs)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EL provides blob data and cell KZG proofs to CL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. Channel is authenticated but content (cell proofs, blob data) must be validated. A buggy EL could provide invalid cell KZG proofs causing invalid sidecar distribution.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer (Sidecar Subscriber)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers receive published sidecars and may also send reconstructed or forwarded sidecars. All P2P input is untrusted and must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer (Sidecar Requester)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated peers request DataColumnSidecars for data availability sampling or reconstruction. Request parameters must be validated (slot range, column indices, custody group membership).

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client (History Query)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application querying pre-merge historical data via JSON-RPC. Explicitly out-of-scope per bug bounty program (publicly exposed API). Included for completeness of trust model but attacks via this vector are not eligible.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer (Block/History Sync)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers providing block data during sync. With EIP-7642 (eth/69) dropping pre-merge fields, peers using the new protocol may provide altered sync data. All received data must be validated against known block hashes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector: a malicious validator can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, or attempt to manipulate fork choice. All gossip messages must be fully validated before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Peer via DevP2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: DevP2P eth/69 protocol (block propagation, transaction relay)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal EL attack vector: a malicious peer node can send invalid blocks, malformed transactions, or attempt eclipse attacks via the DevP2P network. All received data must be fully validated.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Beacon API is out-of-scope per bug bounty. However, proposer lookahead data must be computed deterministically from state to prevent inconsistent duty assignments.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API GetPayloadResponse (BlobsBundle with cell KZG proofs)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CL must validate cell KZG proofs received from EL before constructing and distributing DataColumnSidecars. Invalid proofs from a buggy EL could cause invalid sidecars to be gossiped, potentially triggering consensus failures or data availability issues across the network.

All received sidecars must be validated: KZG proof verification, Merkle inclusion proof verification, column index bounds, slot validity, and proposer signature verification. Malicious peers may send crafted sidecars to cause processing errors or state corruption.
Request parameters must be validated: slot range bounds, column index validity, rate limiting. Malicious peers may send excessive or malformed requests to cause resource exhaustion.
Out-of-scope per bug bounty. Client should return appropriate error for unavailable pre-merge data. No security-critical validation needed beyond standard RPC input sanitization.

All block data received via eth/69 must be validated against canonical block hashes. With pre-merge fields dropped, sync logic must correctly handle the absence of PoW-specific fields (totalDifficulty, etc.) without accepting invalid blocks.

Full block and attestation validation required: signature verification against correct fork version (FULU_FORK_VERSION post-fork), proposer index verification against deterministic lookahead, slot/epoch bounds checking. Post-fork blocks must use Fulu domain for signatures.

Full validation of all received blocks and transactions. With eth/69 dropping pre-merge fields, implementations must not accidentally accept blocks with missing required post-merge fields or reject valid blocks due to changed field expectations.
